===Named after Cruyff===
*[[Johan Cruyff Shield]] (''Johan Cruijff Schaal'' in Dutch), a football trophy in the Netherlands, also referred to as the Dutch [[Super Cup]].
*[[Johan Cruijff Award|Johan Cruyff Award]] or ''[[Dutch Footballer of the Year#Dutch Football Talent of the Year (Young player)|Dutch Football Talent of the Year]]'' (Dutch: Nederlands Voetbal Talent van het Jaar), the title has been awarded in the Netherlands since 1984 for footballers under 21. The award ''Dutch Football Talent of the Year'' was replaced by the [[Johan Cruyff Trophy]] (''Johan Cruijff Prijs'' in Dutch) in 2003.
*[[14282 Cruijff]], the asteroid (minor planet) was named after Cruyff. The [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) officially ratified the naming of Cruijff on 23 September 2010.
*[[Johan Cruyff Institute]], an educational institution, founded by Johan Cruyff, aimed at educating athletes, sport and business professionals in the field of [[sport management]], [[Sports marketing|sport marketing]], football business, [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsorship]] and [[Coach (sport)|coaching]] through a network that currently has five Johan Cruyff Institute (postgraduate and executive education), three Johan Cruyff Academy (graduate education) and five Johan Cruyff College (vocational training).
*''Cruyffista'' (mainly in Spain), a follower/supporter of Cruyff's views (principles) on football development philosophy and sports culture.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/ex-barca-star-jose-mari-bakero-wir-sind-alle-cruyffistas/4228768.html |author=Stier, Sebastian |title=Ex-Barca-Star José Mari Bakero "Wir sind alle Cruyffistas" |publisher=Der Tagesspiegel (tagesspiegel.de) |date=28 May 2011 |access-date=28 August 2016 |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030214432/https://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/wir-sind-alle-cruyffistas-2240308.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Cruyff'sChurch">{{cite web |url=http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/the-church-of-cruyff/ |author=Winner, David |author-link=David Winner (author) |title=The Church of Cruyff: Forever Spreading the Football Gospel |publisher=Bleacher Report Media Lab |date=8 March 2016 |access-date=18 June 2016 |archive-date=2 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702063304/http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/the-church-of-cruyff/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[Johan Cruyff Stadium]] (''Estadi Johan Cruyff'' in Catalan), FC Barcelona's newly constructed stadium is named after Cruyff.
*[[Johan Cruyff Arena]] (''Johan Cruijff Arena'' in Dutch), home stadium of Ajax and previously known as the [[Amsterdam ArenA]].

== In popular culture ==
[[File:2020 Johan Cruijff (Hans Jouta ) (4).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Cruyff's statue at the main entrance of the [[Johan Cruijff Arena]] in Amsterdam]]

In 1976, the Italian-language [[documentary film]] ''Il profeta del gol'' was directed by Sandro Ciotti. The documentary narrates the successes of Johan Cruyff's football career in the 1970s. In 2004, the documentary film ''Johan Cruijff – En un momento dado'' ("''Johan Cruijff – At Any Given Moment''") was made by Ramon Gieling and charts the years Cruyff spent at Barcelona, the club where he had the most profound effect in both a footballing and cultural sense. In 2014, the Catalan-language documentary film ''L'últim partit: 40 anys de Johan Cruyff a Catalunya'' was directed by Jordi Marcos, celebrating 40 years since Johan Cruyff signed for Barcelona in August 1973.

Cruyff had a small hit (number 21 in the charts) in the Netherlands with "[[Oei Oei Oei (Dat Was Me Weer Een Loei)]]". Upon arriving in Barcelona, the Spanish branch of [[Polydor]] decided to release the single in Spain as well, where it was rather popular.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/aug/22/theknowledge.sport|title=Does Shay Given really carry holy water with him at every match?|work=The Guardian|date=22 August 2007|access-date=26 March 2010|location=London, UK|first=James|last=Dart|archive-date=1 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220801134805/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/aug/22/theknowledge.sport|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2004, a public poll in the Netherlands to determine the greatest [[Dutch people|Dutchman]] ("''[[De Grootste Nederlander]]''") named Cruyff the 6th-greatest Dutchman of all time, with Cruyff finishing above [[Rembrandt]] (9th) and [[Vincent van Gogh]] (10th).<ref name="Geschiedenis24_DeGrootsteNederlander_2014">{{cite web |title=De Grootste Nederlander Deel 6: Johan Cruijff |url=http://www.geschiedenis24.nl/speler.program.7055644.html |website=Geschiedenis 24 |access-date=2014-09-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140911001723/http://www.geschiedenis24.nl/speler.program.7055644.html |archive-date=2014-09-11 |url-status=dead |language=nl}}</ref> In 2010, the [[asteroid]] ([[minor planet]]) ''{{ill|14282 Cruijff (2097 P-L)|de|(14282) Cruijff|vertical-align=sup}}'' was named after him. The [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) officially ratified the naming of Cruijff on 23 September 2010. After [[Josef Bican]] and [[Ferenc Puskás]], Cruyff is the third football player to have an asteroid named after him.<ref name="Xs4all_CruijffPlanet">{{cite web |title=Johan Cruijff Continues to Play Football in Outer Space; Minor planet 14282 now named "Cruijff" |url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~carlkop/ecruijff.html |website=Xs4all.nl |access-date=2013-01-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030214438/https://carlkop.home.xs4all.nl/ecruijff.html |archive-date=2023-10-30 |url-status=dead |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Goal_CruyffAsteroid_2010">{{cite web |title=Asteroid Named After Netherlands & Barcelona Legend Johan Cruyff |url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/628/other-top-stories/2010/09/23/2133073/asteroid-named-after-netherlands-barcelona-legend-johan |website=Goal.com |date=2010-09-23 |access-date=2013-01-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140117041324/http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/628/other-top-stories/2010/09/23/2133073/asteroid-named-after-netherlands-barcelona-legend-johan |archive-date=2014-01-17 |url-status=dead |language=en}}</ref>

==Philanthropy==
[[File:2021 Johan Cruyff Court, Molenwijk.jpg|thumb|A Cruyff Court in [[Molenwijk]], Amsterdam Noord. (2021)]]
In the spring of 1997, Cruyff founded the [[Johan Cruyff Foundation]], which is intended to help disadvantaged children and those with special educational needs. He handed over organisational control to others. Apart from the usual sponsor meetings within the framework of the foundation, he was mainly occupied with spending time with children with [[Down syndrome]]. Additionally he founded the Johan Cruyff Academy in 1999,{{sfn|Kok|2022|page=461}} which was soon expanded under the umbrella organisation [[Johan Cruyff Institute]] and extended to several countries. As a programme for 35 athletes as part of the Johan Cruyff University of Amsterdam it has since become a global network and allowed thousands of former players to complete their school or vocational education.<ref>{{cite news|title=Johan Cruyff Institute: About us|newspaper=Johan Cruyff Institute|url=http://cruyffinstitute.org/en/about-us/|publisher=Cruyffinstitute.org|access-date=25 October 2015|archive-date=15 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130615085048/http://cruyffinstitute.org/en/about-us/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Beginning in 2003, the [[Johan Cruyff Foundation]] has provided over 200 [[Cruyff Court]]s in 22 countries, including Israel, Malaysia, Japan, United States, and Mexico, for children of all backgrounds to play street football together.<ref name="CruyffFoundation_Official">{{cite web |title=Johan Cruyff Foundation |url=http://www.cruyff-foundation.org |website=cruyff-foundation.org |access-date=2015-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150607225319/http://www.cruyff-foundation.org/ |archive-date=2015-06-07 |url-status=dead |language=en}}</ref> [[UEFA]] praised the foundation for its positive effect on young people, and Cruyff received the UEFA Grassroots Award on the opening of the 100th court in late 2009.<ref name="UEFA_Cruyff65th">{{cite web |title=Johan Cruyff celebrates his 65th birthday |url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ned/news/newsid=1789173.html |website=UEFA.com |access-date=2015-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130625005951/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ned/news/newsid=1789173.html |archive-date=2013-06-25 |url-status=dead |language=en}}</ref> Cruyff was also an ambassador of the [[Postcode Lottery Group]], which establishes and manages charitable [[Lottery|lotteries]] worldwide to raise funds for social organisations.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.postcodelotterygroup.com/our-people/ambassadors/ | title=Ambassadors }}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Johan Cruijff and Danny Coster 1968.jpg|thumb|left|Cruyff and Danny Coster getting married on 2 December 1968]]

At the wedding of Ajax teammate [[Piet Keizer]], on 13 June 1967, Cruyff met his future wife, Diana Margaretha "Danny" Coster (born 1949). They started dating, and on 2 December 1968, at the age of 21, he married Danny. Her father was Dutch businessman Cor Coster, who also happened to be Cruyff's agent. Cruyff's football career, both as a player and as a manager, was considerably influenced by his family, in particular his wife Danny.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/528411/hard-to-explain |title=Hard to explain |publisher=ESPN FC |last=Bouwes |first=Ernst |quote=Then [[Carles Rexach]] published his book and also claimed that she [Danny] always had a big influence over his career. ... She can also be blamed for [[Netherlands national football team|Holland]] missing out on the World Cup in 1970, and then probably winning it, why not, when Johan had to go on a trip to Milan with Danny to buy shoes for her shop in Amsterdam. He returned too late for the Dutch training camp before their decisive qualifier against Bulgaria and was subsequently dropped. A draw ended all hopes of a trip to Mexico. |date=23 April 2008 |access-date=20 August 2015 |archive-date=20 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151120164627/http://www.espnfc.com/story/528411/hard-to-explain |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/905938/ernst-bouwes-cruyff-rift-tearing-ajax-apart |title=Cruyff rift tearing Ajax apart |publisher=ESPN FC |last=Bouwes |first=Ernst |quote=Following his heart operation in 1991, Danny became stricter in controlling her man. He withdrew as [Netherlands] national coach for the 1994 World Cup in a cloud of arguments after an initial agreement. She probably forbade him to go as it was too dangerous for his health. Several times since, Cruyff has promised to commit to some responsibility, only to resign later with some half-hearted excuse. It's as if she told him to stop being foolish, but he did not dare to say so in public. Danny appears to be very well capable of handling Cruyff. |date=12 April 2011 |access-date=20 August 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304085551/http://www.espnfc.com/story/905938/ernst-bouwes-cruyff-rift-tearing-ajax-apart |url-status=live }}</ref> He and Danny had three children together: Chantal (16 November 1970), Susila (27 January 1972), and [[Jordi Cruyff|Jordi]] (9 February 1974). The family lived in [[Barcelona]] from 1973, with a six-year interruption from December 1981 to January 1988 when they lived in [[Vinkeveen]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Grote Johan Cruijff-hype is in aantocht|url=http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/grote-johan-cruijffhype-is-in-aantocht.htm|publisher=Voetbal International|date=25 October 2015|access-date=26 October 2015|archive-date=17 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117141129/http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/grote-johan-cruijffhype-is-in-aantocht.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Quotes==
{{main|Cruijffiaans}}

Cruyff is the originator of several catchphrases and aphorisms that have entered everyday language, especially in the Netherlands and to some extent in Spain, where they have become proverbial. Several books of collected quotations have become bestsellers in the Netherlands. Biographer Nico Scheepmaker believes Cruyff exerted a universal fascination: even when he was talking nonsense, it was still interesting nonsense. Biographer Auke Kok, conversely, sees the complete absence of common clichés and Cruyff's originality as the reason for his enduring success.{{sfn|Kok|2022|page=466}} For Martin Nowak and Roger Highfield, Cruyff's one-liners oscillate somewhere between the brilliant and the banal.<ref>Martin Nowak & Roger Highfield: ''SuperCooperators: Altruism, Evolution, and Why We Need Each Other to Succeed''. Simon and Schuster, London 2012, p. 100 f.</ref>

* "Coincidence is logical."{{sfn|Kok|2022|page=466}}
* "Every disadvantage has its advantage."<ref name="DWinner_Cruyff'sChurch">{{cite web |author=Winner, David |author-link=David Winner (author) |date=8 March 2016 |title=The Church of Cruyff: Forever Spreading the Football Gospel |url=http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/the-church-of-cruyff/ |access-date=18 June 2016 |publisher=Bleacher Report Media Lab |archive-date=2 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702063304/http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/the-church-of-cruyff/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* "If I wanted you to understand it, I would have explained it better."<ref name="DWinner_Cruyff'sChurch"/>
* "I suspect, that if journalists really understood football they wouldn't be journalists."{{sfn|Kuper|2022|loc=introduction}}
* "Every trainer talks about movement, about running a lot. I say don't run so much. Football is a game you play with your brain."<ref name="DWinner_BrilliantOrange"/>
*"Playing football is very simple but playing simple football is the hardest thing there is."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Henry |first1=Peter |title=20 of Johan Cruyff's best ever quotes |url=https://thefootballfaithful.com/johan-cryuff-20-best-quotes/ |website=The Football Faithful |access-date=14 May 2023 |date=28 April 2023 |archive-date=25 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230325212227/https://thefootballfaithful.com/johan-cryuff-20-best-quotes/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* "Winning is an important thing, but to have your own style, to have people copy you, to admire you, that is the greatest gift."<ref name="JonathanWilson">{{cite web |url=http://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/johan-cruyff-s-legacy-the-whole-of-modern-football_sto5368491/story.shtml |author=Wilson, Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Wilson (writer) |title=Johan Cruyff's legacy? The whole of modern football |publisher=Eurosport (eurosport.co.uk) |date=24 March 2016 |access-date=12 July 2016 |archive-date=29 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629230516/http://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/johan-cruyff-s-legacy-the-whole-of-modern-football_sto5368491/story.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>
* "In my teams, the goalie is the first attacker, and the striker the first defender."<ref name="RamonCalderon_RealMadrid">{{cite web |author=Calderón, Ramón |author-link=Ramón Calderón |date=24 March 2016 |title=Johan Cruyff: Former Real Madrid President Ramon Calderon Pays Tribute To A 'Visionary' |url=http://www.newsweek.com/johan-cruyff-ramon-calderon-barcelona-real-madrid-440545 |access-date=24 July 2016 |work=Newsweek |archive-date=8 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808234642/http://www.newsweek.com/johan-cruyff-ramon-calderon-barcelona-real-madrid-440545 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Illness and death==
{{quote box
| width = 33%
| quote = He has enriched and personified our football. He was an icon of the Netherlands. Johan Cruijff belonged to all of us.
| source = —King [[Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands]] pays tribute following Cruyff's death<ref>{{cite news|title=Reacties op het overlijden van Johan Cruijff|newspaper=NRC|language=nl|date=24 March 2016|url=http://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2016/03/24/live-johan-cruijff-68-overleden|access-date=24 March 2016|archive-date=25 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325041935/http://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2016/03/24/live-johan-cruijff-68-overleden|url-status=live}}</ref>
}}

[[File:2017 Johan Cruijff Vijfje.jpg|thumb|Euro coin, the ''Johan Cruijff Fiver'' issued in 2017, designed by Hennie Bouwe]]

Even as a teenager, Cruyff was a chain smoker (at times smoking 80 cigarettes a day) – a vice he continued into professional football and vehemently defended. He was even said to smoke during halftime breaks.{{sfn|Kuper|2022|page=87}} In February 1991, he suffered a heart attack and had to undergo bypass surgery.{{sfn|Kuper|2022|page=117}} Afterward, he quit smoking and participated in various anti-smoking campaigns; for example, he featured in a Catalan health department advertisement, and symbolically kicked away a cigarette pack.{{sfn|Kuper|2022|page=118}}<ref name="PAHOTV_CruyffNoTobacco_2013">{{cite av media |title=Johann Cruyff, former Netherlands professional soccer player "No Tobacco" |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tBnN6i9lajs |via=[[YouTube]] |publisher=PAHO TV |date=2013-05-07 |language=en}}</ref>

In October 2015, it was revealed that Cruyff had been diagnosed with lung cancer. In February 2016, he announced that he felt as if he were leading 2–0 at halftime in his fight against cancer.<ref name="BBCSport_CruyffCancer_2016">{{cite web |title=Johan Cruyff says he feels '2-0 up' in match against lung cancer |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35568780 |website=BBC Sport |date=2016-02-13 |language=en}}</ref> However, by that time, the cancer had already spread from his lungs to his back and brain. Cruyff died on 24 March 2016, surrounded by his family. His ashes were scattered in the garden of his summer house in El Montanya.{{sfn|Kuper|2022|page=138}}

==Memoirs==
In 2016, Cruyff's posthumously autobiography ''My Turn'' was published, and he also ironically alludes to his legendary trick move. The book, co-written with his long-time ghostwriter Jaap de Groot, was generally met with a very critical reception. Simon Kuper, in a review in the ''[[Financial Times]]'', summed it up as a "missed opportunity". He said it was "full of uninteresting banalities" and argued that the book showcased none of Cruyff's virtues but all his shortcomings and seemed to have been written primarily to settle old scores from his past disputes.<ref name="FinancialTimes_KuperCruyff_2016">{{cite web |last=Kuper |first=Simon |title=Old scores: the message in Johan Cruyff’s memoir |url=https://www.ft.com/content/916566c4-898a-11e6-8cb7-e7ada1d123b1 |website=Financial Times |date=2016-10-06 |language=en}}</ref> 

For [[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting|NOS]], the endless list of administrators and managers, both at Ajax and Barça, with whom Cruyff settled accounts in the book was also a major theme, although Cruyff was also portrayed as mild and understanding towards former associates like Marco van Basten. The figure of Rinus Michels also runs like a [[Leitmotif|''leitmotif'']] through the book: first as a surrogate father, then as a confidant in football tactics, then as the man who may have denied him the coaching position at the 1990 World Cup out of jealousy.<ref name="NOS_CruijffBiografie_2016">{{cite web |title=Johan Cruijff begripvol en venijnig in biografie |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2136216-johan-cruijff-begripvol-en-venijnig-in-biografie |website=NOS |date=2016-10-06 |language=nl}}</ref> In an article for the ''[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]]'', Javier Caceres viewed Cruyff's autobiography as a bland, uninspiring book. He described it as a settling of scores in many places, with few pearls of insight to be found.<ref name="SZ_CaceresCruyff_2016">{{cite web |last=Caceres |first=Javier |title=Revolutionär ohne Diplom |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/johan-cruyff-revolutionaer-ohne-diplom-1.3205898 |website=Süddeutsche Zeitung |date=2016-10-14 |language=de}}</ref> On German [[Deutschlandfunk]] radio, Thomas Jaedicke concluded after reading it that his childhood idol, Cruyff, had also been arrogant and a haughty egotist.<ref name="DLF_CruyffMakel_2016">{{cite web |title=Fußballlegende mit Makel |url=https://www.deutschlandfunkkultur.de/johan-cruyff-fussballlegende-mit-makel-100.html |website=Deutschlandfunk Kultur |date=2016-11-27 |language=de}}</ref>

== Biographies ==
Dutch author Nico Scheepmaker published the first major biography of Johan Cruyff (''Cruijff, Hendrik Johannes, fenomeen'') in 1972; Scheepmaker's book was well received. In 2007, Marcel Rözer published a dual biography of Cruyff and [[Franz Beckenbauer]], ''Beckenbauer & Cruijff: De Keizer en de Verlosser''. Rözer saw significant overlaps and parallels between the two in their backgrounds, careers, and lives; both had become national heroes in their home countries and could even spout nonsense without facing any opposition.

In 2019, the Dutch author Auke Kok published a biography of Cruyff. The biography, a revisionist and critical examination of Cruyff, portrays him as an exceptional athlete but in his private life as someone who engaged in questionable business dealings; while a devoted family man, he was also a notorious womaniser for years, a fact he carefully shielded from the public eye. Also in 2019, Arthur van den Boogaard published the book ''Het laatste seizoen'' about Cruyff's final year at Feyenoord and a retrospective of his playing career. He saw Cruyff as a self-important man with an enormous need for recognition; at the same time, he asserted that in the Netherlands there was a "before Cruyff" and a "after Cruyff", which he likened, analogously to the passing of a [[Rembrandt]]ian era in art.{{sfn|Winner|2008|page=362}} In 2021, Andy Bollen published the book ''Fierce Genius'', in which he also blended a biography with a description of Cruyff's last year as a player for Feyenoord Rotterdam.{{sfn|Bollen|2021|loc=Introduction}}

===Orders and further honours===
* [[File:Order of Orange-Nassau ribbon.svg|x15px]] In 1974, Cruyff was appointed [[Order of Orange-Nassau|Knight of the Order of Orange-Nassau]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Wim Helversteijn|url=https://www.delpher.nl/nl/kranten/view?coll=ddd&identifier=ddd:011236637:mpeg21:a0039|title=Kater van Oranje-ploeg met champagne weggespoeld|date=9 July 1974|work=De Tijd: dagblad voor Nederland|location=delpher.nl|language=nl}}</ref> 
* [[File:Order of Orange-Nassau ribbon - Officer.svg|x15px]] In 2002, Cruyff was promoted to [[Order of Orange-Nassau|Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.delpher.nl/nl/kranten/view?coll=ddd&identifier=KBPERS01:003197009:mpeg21:a00184|title=Cruijff promoveert|date=11 April 2002|work=Algemeen Dagblad|location=delpher.nl|language=nl}}</ref> 
* In November 2003, to celebrate [[UEFA]]'s Jubilee, he was selected as the [[UEFA Jubilee Awards|Golden Player]] of the Netherlands by the [[Royal Dutch Football Association|KNVB]] as their most outstanding player of the past 50 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/Kind=256/newsId=130150.html |title=Golden Players take centre stage |work=[[UEFA]] |access-date=18 March 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312053707/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/Kind%3D256/newsId%3D130150.html |archive-date=12 March 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* On 22 May 2006, Cruyff was presented a Lifetime Achievement Award for his contribution to football by Laureus in their annual [[Laureus World Sports Awards|World Sports Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laureus.com/taxonomy/term/209|title=Johan Cruyff profile|publisher=Laureus|access-date=28 October 2013|archive-date=29 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029220631/http://www.laureus.com/taxonomy/term/209|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In April 2016, Cruyff was posthumously awarded the Laureus Spirit of Sport Award, which was accepted by his son Jordi.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2016/04/19/57155799ca474197058b463e.html|title=Jordi Cruyff accepts award on father's behalf|date=19 April 2016|publisher=Marca.com|access-date=6 August 2017|archive-date=6 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806223640/http://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2016/04/19/57155799ca474197058b463e.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* Cruyff received a lifetime achievement award from the KNVB in August 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/Kind=2/newsId=449866.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108094803/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/Kind%3D2/newsId%3D449866.html |archive-date= 8 January 2009 |title=Kuijt receives Dutch accolade |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=29 August 2006 |access-date=28 October 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ajax.nl/Ajax-Nieuws/Ajax-nieuwsarchief/Ajax-nieuwsartikel/60069/Huntelaar-weer-twee-prijzen-rijker.htm|title=Huntelaar weer twee prijzen rijker|work=Ajax.nl|language=nl|access-date=28 October 2013|archive-date=29 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202619/http://www.ajax.nl/Ajax-Nieuws/Ajax-nieuwsarchief/Ajax-nieuwsartikel/60069/Huntelaar-weer-twee-prijzen-rijker.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>
* On 18 April 2007, Ajax decided to retire the number 14 shirt in honour of Cruyff and in celebration of his birthday.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/Kind=2/newsId=529604.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108111001/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/kind%3D2/newsid%3D529604.html |archive-date= 8 January 2009 |title=Ajax tribute to 'priceless' Cruyff |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=19 April 2007 |access-date=28 October 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In 2010, Cruyff was presented the [[FIFA Order of Merit]] (highest honour awarded by [[FIFA]]) for his contribution to football.<ref name="FIFA_Profile"/>
* In 2010, Cruyff entered in the [[FICTS (Fédération Internationale Cinéma Télévision Sportifs)|FICTS]] "Hall of Fame" and was awarded with "[[Sport Movies & TV – Milano International FICTS Fest|Excellence Guirlande D'Honneur]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportmoviestv.com/2010/10/29/rivera-crujff-tomba-e-giradelli-aprono-qsport-movies-a-tv-2010q/|title=RIVERA, CRUJFF, TOMBA, GIRADELLI E L'INTER APRONO "SPORT MOVIES & TV 2010"|date=29 October 2010|website=Ficts|access-date=25 May 2017|archive-date=19 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819082745/http://www.sportmoviestv.com/2010/10/29/rivera-crujff-tomba-e-giradelli-aprono-qsport-movies-a-tv-2010q/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In 2013, Cruyff was recognised with the [[UEFA President's Award]]<ref name="UEFA President's Award">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0255-0f8e705cf955-a181275bddd8-1000--uefa-president-s-award/|title=UEFA President's Award|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=2 January 2014|access-date=1 June 2017|archive-date=6 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106172739/https://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=2050865.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* On 29 March 2016, the [[Prime Minister of Spain]] awarded Cruyff with the [[Royal Order of Sports Merit|Gold Medal of the Royal Order of Sporting Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.mecd.gob.es/prensa-mecd/actualidad/2016/03/20160229-johan.html | title = El Gobierno de España concede a Johan Cruyff la Medalla de Oro de la Real Orden del Mérito Deportivo a título póstumo | language = es | publisher = mecd.gob.es | access-date = 29 March 2016 | archive-date = 2 April 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160402042835/http://www.mecd.gob.es/prensa-mecd/actualidad/2016/03/20160229-johan.html | url-status = live }}</ref>
* On 25 October 2017, the [[Amsterdam Arena]] was renamed Johan Cruyff Arena.<ref name="Goal_AmsterdamArenaCruyff_2017">{{cite web |title=Amsterdam Arena to be renamed after Johan Cruyff |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/ajax-amsterdam-arena-renamed-johan-cruyff/10orjxvlt40y312dwbbcw93b7z |website=Goal.com |date=2017-04-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007220739/http://www.goal.com/en/news/ajax-amsterdam-arena-renamed-johan-cruyff/10orjxvlt40y312dwbbcw93b7z |archive-date=2017-10-07 |url-status=dead |language=en}}</ref>
